title: Slack teammate progress and evidence outcome stays replayable
description: Acceptance scenario for a redacted Slack teammate thread that posts progress, uses scoped memory, links safe evidence, and finalizes in the same thread.

platform.rationale: Slack contract-lab scenarios must join Ensemble transcript replay with Platform trace and work-envelope evidence before becoming release gates.

assumptions.workflow: A Slack teammate receives a redacted customer thread, posts progress in-thread, recalls scoped memory, gathers safe evidence, proposes/accepts memory, and posts the final outcome in the same thread.
assumptions.correctnessModel: The scenario is correct only when the trace contains same-thread continuity, one progress reply, one final reply, accepted memory lifecycle, safe evidence artifact, and zero replay deltas.
assumptions.threatModel: Raw Slack text, customer identifiers, tool arguments, model responses, connector payloads, and VFS bytes must stay behind permissioned Ensemble and Platform sources.
researchBasis: Existing trajectory replay already gives Maestro deterministic event, score, inspection, and JUnit artifacts.
Slack contract-lab fixtures need real cross-system IDs rather than synthetic-only local session IDs.
Long-horizon Slack teammate evals should score progress, memory lifecycle, evidence handling, and final answer quality together.
